extracted.intended_audience: Prospective contributors to Clarkesworld Magazine (fiction authors, non-fiction writers, and cover artists)
extracted.subtask_description: Submission and publication guidelines for fiction, non-fiction, and art intended for Clarkesworld Magazine; includes formatting, rights, content preferences, and submission processes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fiction word limit
rubrics_metrics.description: 1000-22000 words, no exceptions

rubrics_metrics.name: Fiction pay rate
rubrics_metrics.description: 14¢ per word.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Payment via PayPal or check. (International authors may request wire transfers.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Accepted genres
rubrics_metrics.description: Science fiction and fantasy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: No horror, but dark SF/F is permitted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Language and translations
rubrics_metrics.description: English
rubrics_metrics.guidance: We accept stories from all over the world. Translations are welcome and encouraged, even if the work has been previously published in another language. All rights are restricted to English language unless specifically stated otherwise.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rights claimed
rubrics_metrics.description: We claim first world electronic rights (text and audio), first print rights, and non-exclusive anthology rights for our annual Clarkesworld anthology.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you are unfamiliar with the term 'First Rights,' an explanation can be found on their site. Rights restrictions apply to English language unless otherwise stated.

rubrics_metrics.name: AI writing tools policy
rubrics_metrics.description: We will not consider any submissions translated, written, developed, or assisted by these tools.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Attempting to submit these works may result in being banned from submitting works in the future. (This policy is repeated for fiction, non-fiction, and art: no AI/AI-assisted works.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Simultaneous submissions
rubrics_metrics.description: Simultaneous submissions (having a story under consideration at another market while it is under submission here) are not permitted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Basic quality: well-written language
rubrics_metrics.description: Stories must be well-written.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Language is important. There is no distinction between 'style' and 'substance' or 'story' and 'writing.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Convenience for on-screen reading
rubrics_metrics.description: Make stories convenient for on-screen reading.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Very long paragraphs or typographical trickery may work against you.

rubrics_metrics.name: Suitability for audio
rubrics_metrics.description: Stories should be suitable for audio publication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Stories should be equally effective, but not necessarily the same, in text and audio formats.

rubrics_metrics.name: Science/fantasy rigor and scope
rubrics_metrics.description: Science fiction need not be 'hard' SF; fantasy can be folkloric, contemporary, surreal, etc.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rigor in SF is appreciated; no particular setting, theme, or plot is anathema, but some things are hard sells.

rubrics_metrics.name: Likely hard sells / content to avoid
rubrics_metrics.description: A list of story types that are likely to be rejected (hard sells).
rubrics_metrics.guidance:
The submission page lists the following as likely hard sells:
- zombies or zombie-wannabes (seriously, I’m not kidding)
- sexy vampires, wanton werewolves, wicked witches, or demonic children
- stories about rapists, murderers, child abusers, or cannibals
- stories where the climax is dependent on the spilling of intestines
- stories in which a milquetoast civilian government is depicted as the sole obstacle to either catching some depraved criminal or to an uncomplicated military victory
- stories where the Republicans, or Democrats, or Libertarians, or . . . (insert any political party or religion here) take over the world and either save or ruin it
- stories in which the words 'thou' or 'thine' appear
- talking cats or swords
- stories where FTL travel or time travel is as easy as is it on television shows or movies
- stories about young kids playing in some field and discovering ANYTHING. (a body, an alien craft, Excalibur, ANYTHING).
- stories about the stuff we all read in Scientific American three months ago
- stories about your RPG character’s adventures
- 'funny' stories that depend on, or even include, puns
- stories where the protagonist is either widely despised or widely admired simply because he or she is just so smart and/or strange
- stories originally intended for someone’s upcoming theme anthology or issue (everyone is sending those out, wait a while)
- your trunk stories
- stories that try to include all of the above

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission method (fiction)
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not email or mail submissions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clarkesworld uses an online submissions system that has been designed to streamline the process and improve communication with authors. The submissions form asks for your name, email address, cover letter, story title, word count, genre, and the file containing your story. Guidance for cover letters is linked on the site.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cover letter contents
rubrics_metrics.description: Submissions form requests a cover letter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guidance for what you should and should not include in a cover letter can be found on the site's linked page.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accepted file formats and manuscript format
rubrics_metrics.description: All stories should be in standard manuscript format (modern preferred, classic accepted).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Files may be submitted in .RTF or .DOCX format. No images.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission tracking and confirmation
rubrics_metrics.description: After submitting a story, a tracking number will be displayed on screen and sent via automated email confirmation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you do not receive the email within 24 hours, email them. Your tracking number allows you to monitor submission status via the website; do not lose or share it. Note: some email services may treat tracking emails as spam.

rubrics_metrics.name: Response time and querying policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Average response time is typically under two days, but submissions may be held longer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not send queries about pending submissions until after two weeks have passed. Use your tracking number to check status prior to reaching out. Email queries to Neil at neil@clarkesworldmagazine.com.

rubrics_metrics.name: Revisions and resubmission rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Rules about revisions, resubmissions, and conduct after rejections.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Don't send revisions to a submission unless they have been requested. Don't submit another story for a period of seven days after receiving a rejection. Don't re-submit stories that have been rejected. Do not query for permission. Don't argue with rejection letters.

rubrics_metrics.name: When in doubt follow conservative interpretation
rubrics_metrics.description: If uncertain about any guideline, follow the most conservative interpretation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Questions, concerns, or technical issues can be sent to Neil via email.

rubrics_metrics.name: Confidentiality of personal information
rubrics_metrics.description: An author’s personal information (name, address, email, phone, or secret identity) will not be shared outside editorial staff except in specified situations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exceptions: if compelled by law; if threats are made against staff by the author; if narrators require pronunciation assistance (email only); if year's best editors request inclusion (email only); if the author has instructed them to do so; or if the work submitted is determined to be plagiarized, fraudulent, or otherwise not your own work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission confidentiality and AI training
rubrics_metrics.description: Individual works submitted are treated as confidential material for evaluation only.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: They will not be used to train 'AI' tools of any kind.

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-fiction: scope and pay
rubrics_metrics.description: Clarkesworld is looking for articles of interest to readers of science fiction and fantasy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: They pay 10¢ a word up to a word limit of 2500 words. Acceptable topics include discussions of the genre publishing business, essays on the writing process and reading experience, scientific material useful to SF stories, etc.

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-fiction types they do not want
rubrics_metrics.description: Types of non-fiction they are specifically not interested in receiving.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These are: Reviews (they say there are plenty of other places), Literary Criticism (especially if really just a review), Interviews (handled separately and generally commissioned; do not pitch interviews), Reprints (every article must be original to Clarkesworld).

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-fiction AI policy
rubrics_metrics.description: They are not considering articles written, co-written, or assisted by 'AI' at this time.

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-fiction unlikely topics and anti-patterns
rubrics_metrics.description: Examples of non-fiction subjects that are unlikely to succeed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The page lists several examples that generally won't work: explanations of why your favorite genre is best and others rubbish; attempts to categorize genre literature; convention reports; articles about why awards 'got it wrong'; articles inciting blogosphere rage; articles that make sweeping generalizations from few observations; manifestos for new literary movements; personal experience of alien abduction; and articles that purport to explain broad industry conspiracies without evidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-fiction style preferences
rubrics_metrics.description: Preferred writing style and tone for non-fiction articles.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Keep yourself out of the article; aim for objective analysis rather than personal journalism. They are not an academic journal—pitch for a general audience. Footnotes are fine (not included in word count). No 'interviews in disguise' (don't write something that is functionally an interview). Don't 'bait' the audience with rage-inducing content. Know your topic and avoid factual errors; they can arrange fact-checking if needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: What non-fiction editors like
rubrics_metrics.description: Qualities that increase chances of acceptance for non-fiction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: They like articles that are thoughtful, in-depth, and well-written; cover subjects they haven't covered before; include accompanying illustrations (check copyright); and show a clear passion for the subject matter.

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-fiction submissions process
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not send completed non-fiction articles; send a query letter instead.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Send a query with subject header 'NONFICTION QUERY: [title or concept]' to nonfiction@clarkesworldmagazine.com. There are no response times; they will generally only respond to queries they wish to follow-up on. A follow-up email is not a guarantee of publication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cover art rights and payment
rubrics_metrics.description: Cover usage rights and payment for artists.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The cover for each issue is used across all editions (online, ebook, digital subscription, and print). Rights are restricted to those covers and marketing materials for that specific issue; all other rights remain with the artist. Payment is $600 and two copies of the print edition. The artist’s bio and link to their online portfolio will be included in the issue featuring their art.

rubrics_metrics.name: What kind of art they want
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance on style and storytelling for cover art.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Genre art doesn’t have to look genre. They consider cover art to be its own story and do not look for pieces that overlap with that issue’s fiction—tell a story through your art. Unpublished portfolio work will be considered; they prefer digital or traditional 2D paintings and illustrations. Color artwork is preferred. They have bought B&W art but it's a hard sell. No photography, photomanipulations, or 'AI'/'AI-assisted' works.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cover text and composition constraints
rubrics_metrics.description: Be aware of where text will appear on finished covers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Author names and the magazine header will appear on all finished covers. If your art contains crucial elements that appear in these locations, it probably won't work for them. If enthusiastic about a piece with this problem, they may ask for changes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Art technical specifications
rubrics_metrics.description: Technical requirements for cover artwork.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Artwork must be available in a 300dpi .tif or other high-resolution format. Landscape covers measure 11" wide by 8.5" high. (Portrait 5.5" wide by 8.5" high.) Artwork for covers must include a 1/4" bleed. Do not crop your own artwork if it goes outside these margins. Artwork must be friendly to resizing; something that looks great at full-size must remain impressive at 350px tall on their website.

rubrics_metrics.name: Previously used artwork policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Previously published cover art policy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: They will not consider artwork that has been previously used for magazine or book covers. Exceptions are rare and by invitation only. Unpublished portfolio work will be considered.

rubrics_metrics.name: Art submissions process
rubrics_metrics.description: How artists should submit work for consideration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Artists should send the URL of their online gallery or portfolio to Neil Clarke (art@clarkesworldmagazine.com). Do not attach images to the message. They will get in touch if interested in licensing a particular piece. Portfolios will be periodically reviewed; no need to send updates unless you change the location of your portfolio.
